reviews.title: Quizás la peor app de cuidado de mascotas
reviews.text: Primero para crear un perfil de cuidador tienes que pasar por veinte mil pasos, que si fotos, que si reseñas, que si Facebook etc, etc..Luego con las reservas se ponen muy pesados, el dueño tiene que firmar documentos, facilitar mil cosas o sea solo falta ir al notario para completar un trabajo. Cuando ya has reservado con alguien, te mandan mensajes todo el rato para que mandes actualizaciones del trabajo cada día y para completar la reserva te piden escanear un código QR del dueño(???). Total, una app muy estresante para que al final de cada trabajo te quiten el 25%!!!!!Hay apps mucho mejores que esta que ofrecen más cosas y te cobran mucho menos.

reviews.title: Don’t Recommend
reviews.text: I’ve been looking for work on Petbacker. I completed all the qualifications weeks ago. I’ve been Housesitting and dog sitting for other companies in the past and this app only gets a few leads once every couple of weeks and the actual requests don’t seem to be professional or legitimate. They want you to call them on their personal phone and it seems to be a fake number and don’t follow up through the app.  I’ve received no confident inquiries and it seems to be a waste of time and energy.

reviews.title: Significant Pricing Disconnect and "Expat Tax" Issues
reviews.text:
Buyers be warned! The app is predatory towards both client markets and providers (read reviews and a ton of hidden fees for providers which drive up costs to consumers). The app itself functions okay, but the marketplace logic is completely broken, especially for users in developing countries. I found the quote system to be a race to the top for the most unrealistic pricing. I was receiving bids for $80+ US per day on what should cost around $20-$40 (and that’s for four animals) for basic pet sitting in the Philippines. The rates are logically inverted when you consider the sitter’s role includes private upscale accommodation, high-speed internet, and full amenities for a job that outside of a couple potty breaks and a couple feedings basically consists of chilling out, eating your food, watching your TV, and doomscrolling short-video on your high-speed internet which is often hard to come by here in the Philippines.

It feels like the app's algorithm or 'suggested rates' along with their taxes and fees encourage sitters to charge Western-tier prices (or higher) for services that attempt to re-configure the local economy, leading to a lot of time wasted declining 'lofty' proposals that don't reflect the local economy at all. I eventually found several highly qualified, experienced professionals outside the app for 1/4 of the cost. If you're an expat or moving to the region, be prepared to do a lot of vetting to avoid getting fleeced. The app needs better localized pricing gua
